# PagedView

<!-- Generated by scripts/sync-component-docs.mjs from ai/component-catalog.json and ai/component-composition.json. Do not edit; run `npm run catalog:sync`. -->

`@kerfjs/ui:paged-view` · Kerf UI · component · Navigation

A region that pages horizontally between full-size panes, with compact page dots floating in a pill at the bottom: touch swipes and trackpad scrolls snap to a page, and the dots work by click and arrow keys. The application owns the current page.

## When to use

Offer two to five alternative presentations of one sidebar or panel region (charts, gauges, a list) one at a time, with swipe, trackpad, dot, and keyboard paging and an app-persisted page.

- A sidebar or panel region shows one of a few alternative presentations at a time and people page between them by swiping, scrolling sideways, or clicking dots: render PagedView with pages and the controlled page, wire wirePagedViews, and set page from onPageChange.
- The chosen page should persist per viewer: store the id onPageChange reports.

**Not when:**

- Do not use it for named destinations people pick by name; use a TabBar with TabPanels or a SegmentedControl.
- Do not use it for a hierarchy or a drill-down flow; use NavStack or ColumnExplorer.
- Do not build a scroll-snapped pager or page dots by hand; use PagedView.

**Alternatives:**

- [TabBarItem](./tabs.md) (semantic-alternative) — Use TabBar and TabPanel when each page has a visible name people choose by.
- [SegmentedControl](./segmented-control.md) (nearest) — Use a SegmentedControl above the content to switch between a few named views of the same data.
- [ColumnTrack](./column-track.md) (nearest) — Use ColumnTrack layout="paged" for a board of columns with the next one peeking in.

## Imports

- JavaScript: `@kerfjs/ui/paged-view` — exports `PagedView`, `PagedViewProps`, `PagedViewPage`.
- CSS: the browser build of `@kerfjs/ui/paged-view` pulls its CSS automatically; import `@kerfjs/ui/paged-view.css` manually only without the `browser` export condition.
- Wiring: `wirePagedViews` from `@kerfjs/ui/wire-paged-views` (required).
- Declared side effects: browser-condition-css.

## Props

Exact prop names and types: [`@kerfjs/ui/paged-view`](../public-api-signatures-v1.md#kerfjsuipaged-view) in `public-api-signatures-v1.md`. Do not infer props from examples.

**Variants (configure, do not restyle):**

- two to five pages
- a single page (no dots)
- narrow sidebar width

## Composition

- Parents: any.
- Contexts: `application-ui`.
- Children: unrestricted.

## State and wiring

**The app owns:** the controlled page id and its persistence; the pages, their labels, and their content.

**Wiring:** `wirePagedViews` is required.

- Use wirePagedViews as documented.

## Geometry

Margin: none · border: none · padding: none (layout role: navigation). `self` means the component already owns it — do not add wrapper padding, margin, or borders around it.

- The view fills its region; each page is the full width and height of the region and scrolls vertically on its own. Page content owns its inset (a ContentItem, List, or ListInsetText); add no wrapper padding.
- The dots float in a chrome-material pill fixed 8px above the bottom edge, so content scrolls beneath them; each page ends with block-end padding equal to the pill plus its offsets, so its last item scrolls clear.

## Accessibility

- The dots are a tablist named by label; each dot is a tab named "Page 2 of 3: \<page label>" (localize it with the pageLabel template, which fills {index}, {count}, and {label}) with aria-selected and aria-controls, and only the current dot is in the Tab order.
- Each page is a tabpanel named by its dot; pages other than the current one are inert, so focus and assistive technology stay on the visible page.
- With wirePagedViews: Left and Right on a focused dot move to the previous and next page (mirrored right to left), Home and End to the first and last.
- Paging slides smoothly, and jumps without animation when prefers-reduced-motion is set. The current dot is a wider pill, so the state does not rest on color alone; forced colors paint it Highlight.

The component renders controls inside it, so it cannot sit in the zones of a component whose root is a control or link. (`KUI-V014`)

## Styling boundary

The component owns its own styles. Configure it through its props and variants; do not override its internals.

Public class hooks (select for layout placement only, never to change the component's look): `kui-paged-view`, `kui-paged-view__viewport`, `kui-paged-view__page`, `kui-paged-view__dots`, `kui-paged-view__dot`.

Never put `kui-paged-view`, `kui-paged-view__viewport`, `kui-paged-view__page`, `kui-paged-view__dots`, `kui-paged-view__dot` on an element you write; render `PagedView` instead (`KUI-L103`).

Everything else is internal: `kerf-ui-analyze` reports private or unknown `.kui-*` selectors (`KUI-L001`, `KUI-L010`), unknown or private tokens (`KUI-L002`, `KUI-L012`), and any application rule that restyles the component, forced dimensions included (`KUI-L019`).
